nom: La Roche-Posay Toleriane Double Repair Face Moisturizer with Niacinamide

segments.oily: Reviewers who describe their skin as oily or shine-prone say the cream absorbs without leaving a greasy film, though one warns its fairly thick texture may not suit very oily skin as well as lighter formulas.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry to very dry skin, including some with medical conditions or pregnancy-related dryness, mostly report the cream relieves flaking and tightness, though a few with extremely dry skin found it didn't moisturize enough on its own, especially in cold or dry climates.
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin, including some who are also acne-prone, report it hydrates without breaking them out or leaving oily patches.
segments.sensitive: Reviewers with sensitive skin, including several with rosacea, overwhelmingly describe the fragrance-free formula as calming and non-irritating, though one reviewer with sensitive, redness-prone skin found it stung and worsened her redness even after six weeks of use.
segments.mature: A couple of reviewers over 50, including one with menopausal skin whose dermatologist recommended it for rosacea, report it keeps dry, mature skin comfortable and reduces redness, with one calling it the best drugstore buy for mature skin.

concerns.aging: A couple of reviewers with mature or menopausal skin report their skin looks more hydrated and youthful-looking after overnight use, though anti-aging effects are mentioned only incidentally alongside hydration and redness improvements.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers, including several with dry or very dry skin, report the lightweight formula absorbs quickly and keeps skin hydrated through the day; however, some with extremely dry skin found it pills and doesn't moisturize enough on its own in cold or dry climates, needing to reapply or layer a heavier product.
concerns.redness: Many reviewers, including several with rosacea, report the cream calmed redness, cleared papules, or reduced flare-ups within days to weeks; one reviewer with sensitive, redness-prone skin, however, found it stung and left her skin visibly more red even after six weeks of use.
concerns.barrier: Several reviewers describe the niacinamide and ceramides as repairing or strengthening a compromised skin barrier, with less dryness and irritation after regular use; one reviewer with very dry skin, though, saw no improvement in her skin barrier or moisture levels after several weeks.
concerns.spots: A couple of reviewers used the moisturizer alongside dark-spot or acne-scar treatments and reported visible fading of post-acne marks within about two weeks, and one describes it as helping fade hyperpigmentation, though most reviews focus on hydration rather than spot-fading specifically.
concerns.blemishes: The majority of reviewers, including many with acne-prone skin, report the moisturizer does not clog pores or cause new breakouts and in some cases reduced existing breakouts; however, one reviewer developed recurring cystic acne on her nose over a year and a half of use, and another broke out around the mouth after a few weeks.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers with oily or shine-prone skin generally say it absorbs without leaving a greasy or oily look by day's end; one reviewer, though, felt its fairly thick texture may not suit very oily skin as well as lighter formulas.

aspects.libelle: Pills or balls up when layered or rubbed
Tube or bottle wastes leftover product
Price felt high relative to the size
Layers well under makeup and sunscreen

extraits.texte: I'm decades away from my teens. This moisturizer brought the memories of troublesome skin back-- but worse! Toleriane Double Repair has been causing cystic pimples on my nose. I would get one like every other month or so. I never had this type of pimple as a teens, mind you - I had to look this up. Cystic acne is close to boils - it's super painful, large, and lasts about 2 weeks long. Before I started using this product, I was using RoC Retinal Line Smoothing Max Hydration (fragrance free) Cream 🧡 for 3+ years. Not once did I get 'cystic acne'. Looking to save a buck, I'm like, This moisturizer is a little cheaper, and very popular, let me give it a try. I've been using it for about 1.5 years. In that time, I've probably had 6 cystic nose pimples. They're so awful, like having a welt on your nose that's bright red and oh so painful. You just have to ride the thing out too. 😢 Also, the "pilling" of the moisturizer is 100% real. I could almost deal with the moisturizer wiping off my face in chunklets,... but this latest cystic experience was so unpleasant. No More! I'm definitely going back to my trusty RoC Retinal Line Smoothing Max Hydration Cream. I'm using the remainder of mine as glorified hand lotion. Also, the RoC Retinal Line Smoothing Max Hydration Cream comes in such lovely jars that you can wash them out and reuse them for all sorts of things. They're very pretty.

I really tried to like this product but even after 6 weeks it is still aggravating my redness. You can see I applied this product to the left of my face (in the photo it appears on your right). I feel like I can see a marked redness from this product alone. I naturally have sensitive skin, redness, and acne. I have a history of being on Accutane so my skin can be fairly dry and flaky despite the humid conditions I live in. I use other LP products and love them, but this one slightly stings when applying and still aggravates my skin even after going through most of the product to give a fair review. At first I really thought maybe I just needed to give the product time, but I don’t think it’s a good fit for my skin. I need a product that is moisturizing without being too heavy as I am prone to clogged pores and I find I get greasy easy living in Hawaii. I thought the niacinamide might help my post acne dark spots and never reacted to this ingredient before. It doesn’t sting elsewhere on my body, so I’ll use the rest of the container elsewhere. Really hoping I can find a product that works for my skin…

extraits.titre: Perfect for oily, sensitive types and damaged skin barrier BUT pills if you don't know how to use it
extraits.texte: Don't get me wrong: it'll never break you out, it'll repair your skin barrier, and fade hyperpigmentation to even out your skin tone but it barely moisturizes since I have extremely dry skin and it pills a lot (creates crumbs on your face). You need to apply it on damp skin and rub it in extremely well, or apply it right after something wet like a serum or aloe vera in order for it to not pill. You could also just use it as a dedicated nighttime moisturizer if you don't want to risk someone seeing you pill at all. It'd be perfect for someone with an oily, sensitive skin type and they would not have much issue like I did. Where you live also depends because in tropical humid climates like Singapore, Mexico, or the Philippines, it absorbed into my skin easily and never pilled but the second I moved to a cold, dry climate in California, it pilled like crazy and didn't moisturize enough. If La Roche Posay changed the formulation to make it absorb better and never pill (or maybe added more moisture with hyaluronic acid/panthenol), this would probably be the best moisturizer on the market.

extraits.titre: Disappointing, after I heard great things
extraits.texte: I have very dry and sensitive skin. I have to make sure I use a good moisturizer to get the proper skin texture for myself. I heard great things about this product and wanted to try. It does have a non-greasy like texture to the product and you only need a little bit. I initially liked it at first. It went on smoothly and it made my skin feel a little bit more soft. But after using it for a couple of weeks, it actually made my skin breakout, mainly around the mouth area. I also didn’t see an improvement in my skin barrier or the moisture content. Though it may work for other skin types. It just wasn’t a win for me. As for the value of your money, it is on the pricier side so beware if you do have sensitive skin.

extraits.titre: A Staple in My Skincare Routine – Especially for Travel & Dry Skin!
extraits.texte: This face cream has truly earned a permanent spot in my skincare routine. The texture is soft and velvety with absolutely no scent, which I really appreciate—especially since my skin can be sensitive. It dispenses easily, and the consistency is just right: not too greasy or heavy, but also not too light. It strikes that perfect balance and soaks in beautifully. One of my favorite things is how well it layers under makeup. It creates a smooth base without pilling or feeling slick, and it works just as well at night as it does during the day. I travel constantly—including ultra-long 23-hour flights from LAX to Hong Kong—and this cream always comes with me in my carry-on. Airplane cabins are incredibly drying, and applying this mid-flight makes a noticeable difference in keeping my skin hydrated and comfortable. I’ve also been in a cold climate for the past three months, and this has significantly helped with my dry skin. For reference, I’m over 50 with dry, menopausal skin, and my dermatologist actually recommended this for my rosacea. I’ve seen a substantial improvement in redness and overall skin comfort since using it consistently. It’s gentle, effective, and reliable. I will absolutely continue using this as a routine staple and highly recommend it—especially if you travel often, live in a dry climate, or struggle with sensitive or mature skin.

extraits.auteur: Home, Style, Beauty and Everyday Finds
extraits.titre: Good everyday moisturizer for all skin types
extraits.texte: I have dry, sensitive skin and have been using this morning and night for a few weeks. What I like most is that it feels lightweight but still keeps my skin comfortable throughout the day. Some moisturizers for sensitive skin feel heavy or greasy, but this one absorbs quickly and layers well over serum without pilling. It’s fragrance fee, oil free and doesn’t irritate my skin or make me red, which is a huge plus. My skin feels softer and more balanced after using it consistently. I also like that it works well under makeup during the day. Pros: - Lightweight but hydrating - Good for sensitive skin - No strong scent - Absorbs quickly - Works well under makeup Cons: - May not be rich enough for super dry skin in winter - Price is a little high for the size Overall, I think it’s a solid everyday moisturizer if you want something gentle, simple and reliable without feeling heavy.

I bought this because I have Rosacea subtype 2 (papular/pustule - so basically tiny, painful pimple-like bumps that DO NOT respond to any type of acne treatment). I still can't figure out if I have triggers & nothing seems to help when I have flares. During these flares, my moisture barrier is non-existent and my skin becomes so dry that it peels & scales. I bought this on a whim & cannot believe the difference in just a few days. My cheeks are still a little rosy, but I have ZERO pustules & the broken capillaries seem to be gone as well. It even got rid of the blackheads on my nose that I can NEVER get rid of. If this continues to help then I'm a customer for life. The 1st pic is from a week ago & the 2nd is right now.
